author: deepseek-ai
body:
# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

title: heydamir/unslop
author: heydamir
body:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

title: zortos293/Lichii
author: zortos293
body:
⚠️ Lichii has no official website ⚠️

> [!CAUTION] > **Lichii has no official website.** The only site run by this project is the **game compatibility website, [lichii.zortos.me](https://lichii.zortos.me)**, for compatibility reports only. Download Lichii **only** from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Any other "Lichii" website or download (such as lichii.org) is not ours and may contain malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)).

# Lichii Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the [Lichii game compatibility website](https://lichii.zortos.me) to find games and compare community compatibility reports. ## Downloads and setup Download Lichii only from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Lichii has no other download site: archives offered elsewhere, such as lichii.org, are not built by this project, and one has been reported to install malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)). On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Only use games and system files you have legally obtained. Games, keys and firmware are not included. ### Existing saves and settings Lichii uses its own profile: `%APPDATA%\lichii` on Windows, and the `lichii` directories under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux and macOS. Without XDG overrides, these are `~/.local/share/lichii`, `~/.config/lichii` and `~/.cache/lichii`. An existing portable `user/` directory still takes priority and is not imported or changed by the wizard. On the first non-portable GUI launch, Lichii offers to import Eden and other detected emulator profiles. Back up `%APPDATA%\eden` first on Windows, or the old data, config and cache directories on Unix, and close the source emulator. Choose **Keep Old Data** to copy without changing the source, then check your saves and relaunch. Existing destination data is retained in backup directories rather than merged. Move also retains a source backup until you remove it yourself; Link deliberately shares settings and saves. Paths outside the imported data root remain shared and unchanged. An interrupted import offers recovery on the next launch. `eden-cli`, including `--help` and `--version`, refuses to initialize configuration until you import or explicitly choose **Start fresh** in the GUI. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee. Browse [community compatibility reports](https://lichii.zortos.me/reports) for results with each player's build and setup. Desktop reporting requires a build containing [PR #303](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/303) and is not available in build 88. In builds that include it, play and stop a Switch 2 game, then right-click that game and choose **Submit compatibility report**. Only the latest session in the current Lichii process is eligible. Confirm the matching website catalog entry and review the editable machine, game, setup, and enabled add-on details prefilled where available. Check the public preview and give explicit consent before submitting. Nothing uploads automatically, and the native v1 reporter does not read or upload logs or files. When [reporting an issue](https://github.com/zortos293/Eglantine/issues), include: - The exact build, game version, CPU, GPU and driver version. - Relevant settings and steps to reproduce the problem. - A screenshot and the log from the affected session, after checking it for personal information. Do not upload game files, keys, firmware or private account information. ## Building and contributing See the [build guide](docs/Build.md), [user documentation](docs/user/README.md) and [coding guidelines](docs/Coding.md). Some inherited documentation and internal build target names still use upstream names. The GUI build target remains `yuzu`; its output is `lichii.exe` on Windows and `lichii` on other desktop platforms. Keep changes focused and distinguish code-level checks from actual gameplay testing. ## Artwork Art created by YOB (yobslab) The supplied Lichii logo, icon and library artwork are in [dist/branding](dist/branding). Windows, Linux and macOS icon resources are generated from that artwork by [Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1](tools/Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1). ## Support Lichii Lichii is free and stays free. If you want to help, you can donate in crypto. Donations help pay for the AI tools and build machines used to develop this open-source project faster. **Solana (SOL)** ```text JepEjfyWjGjhJvHSrqj52KtLjcbbbmUh1iGqerYBF4w ``` **Ethereum (ETH)** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` **Bitcoin (BTC)** ```text bc1qcvxdpf4qvdhqp8ee4s355cjmxrzsphsdwpl8w4 ``` **BNB Smart Chain (BNB)** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` **Polygon** ```text 0x055ABa1b80Bc35C836Ce7E9F47c2b3d6C75b5534 ``` Send each coin on its matching network. Coins sent on the wrong network can't be recovered. > [!NOTE] > Donations are voluntary gifts and are non-refundable. A donation does not buy any product, service, perk, early access, exclusive build, priority support or say in the project. Every release stays free and public for everyone. ## Credits and license Lichii inherits the work of the Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi projects and their contributors, including Eglantine's original developer Camille LaVey. Original copyright notices and third-party licenses are retained. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt) and the source files for applicable license terms.

title: NotRexed/Hookshot
author: NotRexed
body:
Hookshot

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.

Status | Install and play | In-game menu | Problems | Build from source | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows or Linux program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**.
> [!WARNING] > Some users report the file in releases to be a Trojan - it is not. Feel free to run it through any antivirus software Discord: https://discord.gg/DVQQJphbBf
> [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy. Everything the build creates (`hookshot.exe`, the generated code, the shader caches and your > saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. ## Project status Experimental. Most testing so far has been around the start of the game. Players have reported on many PCs since: the table says what works and what does not yet. | What | Status | |---|---| | Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around | ✅ Works | | Sound, controller, keyboard and saves | ✅ Works | | In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling | ✅ Works | | Flicker (the picture flashing too bright while moving) | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ([#645](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/pull/645)) | | Ground fog vanishing when looking down | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ([#638](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/pull/638)) | | Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) | ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed | | Stutter when entering new areas | ⚠️ Still happens the first time you visit a place. The next visits are smooth | | Performance | ⚠️ Depends on the PC: some reach a steady 60 fps, others stay below it, more so in Hyrule Field | | Hyrule Field, Castle Town, Kakariko and the dungeons | ⚠️ Players got there, with open bugs: striped shadows in Hyrule Field ([#468](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/468)), some crashes ([#317](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/317), [#648](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/648)) | | Ultrawide and 4:3 | ⚠️ The 3D keeps its shape, but the HUD is stretched and the picture is softer | | NVIDIA cards | ✅ Works. The most tested | | AMD cards | ⚠️ Some tested: reports from the RX 6600, RX 7800 XT and RX 7900 XTX. Known issue: the game loses the GPU in the Deku Tree on the RX 6600 ([#708](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/708), [#614](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/614)) | | Intel cards | ❓ Few reports, many of them black screens or crashes ([#17](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/17)) | | Cards without mesh shaders (such as AMD RX 5000 and older) | ❌ Not supported: parts of the picture are missing. Since v2.0.6 a fallback runs the mesh programs as compute shaders on cards with buffer device addresses ([#640](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/640)); it leaves out the mesh draws that take their count from a buffer | | Linux | ✅ Works with the AppImage. Tested on several distributions (CachyOS, Fedora, Bazzite, SteamOS) and cards, with open problems on some AMD cards ([#604](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/604), [#528](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/528)) | ## Install and play The game does not come ready-made: Hookshot Builder builds it on your PC from your copy. You do this once. After that you start the game from its launcher, which also updates it. ### What you need - **Your copy of the game at the supported version:** program `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, build `e0f3ccfa`. Other versions do not work. A `.nup` file, or the `romfs` and `exefs` folders. - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...) and a CPU with AVX2. The Linux AppImage needs AVX2; on Windows, and in a build from source, a CPU without it gets a game built for what it has, a little slower. - A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 series or newer, AMD Radeon RX 6000 series or newer, or Intel Arc. On Linux, Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. Cards without mesh shaders are not supported. - 8 GB of video memory (VRAM) or more is recommended. Cards with less can use the in-game menu's lower Quality presets. - 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB. - About 60 GB free while building, on an SSD if you can: a hard drive makes the build much slower. You can build on one anyway; the builder says so first. - An internet connection for the download. Nothing else to install: the builder brings its own compiler and tools. ### On Windows 1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/latest) and download `HookshotBuilder.exe`. 2. Run it. It downloads the rest of Hookshot Builder (about 500 MB), checks it, and opens it. 3. Pick your game. The builder looks for `.nup` files in your Downloads, Desktop and Documents folders and lists them under **Found on this PC**. Not listed? Press **Browse…**, drop the file on the window, or choose **romfs and exefs folders**. The builder checks that it is the right version. 4. Under **Install the game to**, keep the folder (`Games\Hookshot` in your user folder) or press **Change**. Choose the **Game language**. 5. Press **Build the game**. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. You can use your PC in the meantime. 6. When it says **Your game is ready**, press **Play**. The **Desktop shortcut** and **Start menu entry** boxes are ticked: untick them if you don't want them. Next time, start the game from the Hookshot shortcut, or `hookshot.exe` in the game folder. That is the launcher: it has **Play**, and **Update** when a newer release is out. The first start prepares the game's shaders, which takes a while. Later starts are faster. ### On Linux 1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/latest) and download `Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage`. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside. 2. Allow it to run as a program. In most file managers: right-click it, open **Properties**, and turn on "Allow executing file as program" (the words differ between desktops). Or in a terminal: `chmod +x Hookshot-*-x86_64.AppImage`. 3. Double-click it. The Hookshot Builder window opens. 4. Under **Game files**, choose **.nup file** or **romfs and exefs**, then press **Browse** to pick them. The builder checks the version. 5. Under **Save the game to**, keep `~/Games/Hookshot` or choose another folder. Choose a **Language**. 6. Press **Build**. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. 7. When it says "Your game is ready", press **Play**. The game is also added to your applications menu as "Hookshot". That entry, and `hookshot` in the game folder, open the launcher: **Play**, and **Update** when a newer release is out. Keep the AppImage where it is: the launcher uses it to update. The same AppImage also builds and starts the game without opening the window, for a machine you reach over SSH or for a script: see [Linux, the AppImage from the command line](#build-from-source). For fast GPU memory imports on Linux, the game user needs read/write access to `/dev/udmabuf` (the kernel's `udmabuf` module). Without it, Hookshot falls back to host-pointer imports, which can be much slower on AMD/RADV; permission errors produce a warning on stderr and in `hookshot_log.txt`. Check `ls -l /dev/udmabuf` and `id`. An administrator can add you to the device's owning group, then you must log out and back in. Only use that group if access to its other devices is intended: `kvm` also grants virtualization access. For an active local desktop session using systemd-logind, prefer a device-specific rule in `/etc/udev/rules.d/70-hookshot-udmabuf.rules`: `SUBSYSTEM=="misc", KERNEL=="udmabuf", TAG+="uaccess"` (before `73-seat-late.rules`). This grants access to the active local user, not SSH or service users. For those, an administrator can instead create a dedicated `udmabuf` group, add only the game user, and use `SUBSYSTEM=="misc", KERNEL=="udmabuf", GROUP="udmabuf", MODE="0660"` in that file. Reload with `sudo udevadm control --reload-rules` and apply with `sudo udevadm trigger --action=add /sys/class/misc/udmabuf`; restart the session/service after a group change. If the device is absent, the distribution must provide/load the module first (`sudo modprobe udmabuf`). Do not run the game as root or make the device world-writable. ### Updating When a new release is out, the launcher says "Update available". Press **Update**: in `hookshot.exe` on Windows, or in `hookshot` (or the AppImage) on Linux. It downloads only the parts that changed and builds the game again in the same folder. The build files of the last build are gone by then (see [Where the files go](#where-the-files-go)), so an update takes about as long as the first build. Your saves and settings are kept. What changed is on the [Releases page](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases).
What an update keeps and replaces, and updating from the command line To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the `user` folder in the game folder on Windows, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux. | Kept | Replaced | |---|---| | Your saves (`user`, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux) | The game in `bin` and its files | | `hookshot_options.ini`, the in-game menu's choices and your controls | `image.bin` and the shader list | | `hookshot_env.txt` | `language.txt`, written again with the game's language | | `mods` | | The game files the first build read are kept in the game folder, so an update does not need your `.nup` again. From a clone: `git pull`, then `python -I nx2/make_game.py --update `. The Linux AppImage does the same with `--update `.
### Latest development build Want a fix before it is in a release? The [latest development build](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/tag/nightly) is made from `main` after every change, with the same files as a release. It is untested and may break your saves or settings: copy them first (see above). - **Windows:** download `HookshotBuilder.exe` from it and start it from a terminal as `HookshotBuilder.exe --tag nightly` (without `--tag nightly` it installs the latest release instead). - **Linux:** download `Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage` from it and use it as above. To go back, install the [latest release](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/releases/latest) the usual way. ### Where the files go - The build reads your game and never changes it. It writes to the folder you choose and to the builder's own folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder` on Windows, `~/.cache/hookshot-builder` on Linux. - The romfs is hard-linked instead of copied where the disk allows it. - The build files (about 4 GB: the translated code and the compiled objects) are deleted once the game is ready. None of them are needed to play. To keep them, so that an update compiles only what changed, set the environment variable `HOOKSHOT_KEEP_BUILD_FILES=1` for the builder; on Windows, **Free up space** on the "Your game is ready" page then deletes them when you want. The build files folder can be moved before a build (**Change**, **Default**). - Saves: the `user` folder in the game folder on Windows, `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux (a `user` folder from an earlier Linux build is moved there once). `--user ` puts them somewhere else ([command line arguments](#running-the-game-from-the-command-line)). To carry on with a save from an emulator (Lichii, Eglantine, Orchid, ...) or NX2navi, or to take yours there, see [using a save from an emulator](docs/saves.md). - To uninstall, delete the game folder, the builder's folder and the shortcuts. ### If something goes wrong | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | Where is the log? | `hookshot_log.txt` in the game folder holds the last run. The four runs before are `hookshot_log.1.txt` (the last) to `.4.txt`. Started from a terminal, the game prints there instead. Every 600 frames it has a `vk: status:` line: the video memory in use of what the driver allows, and DLSS's details while it draws; `vk: over the driver's video-memory allowance` says when the game passed it | | Linux Builder Play closed before the game log appeared | After the game exits, check `hookshot_startup.log` in the game folder for up to 64 KiB of startup stderr and its exit status. | | "Hookshot supports build e0f3ccfa" or "This version isn't supported" | Check that you chose the right game with its update installed | | The game opens and closes, or the log says "device lost" | Update your graphics driver. On AMD cards there are known crashes ([#708](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/708), [#614](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/614)) | | Parts of the picture are missing, or a message says your card has no mesh shader support | The card or its driver has no mesh shaders. Update the driver; older cards are not supported ([#640](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/640)) | | AMD: blocky textures, solid rectangles in the sky or unusually dark courtyard surfaces | Try the [RGBA8 texture workaround](#amd-texture-workaround). It uses more graphics memory | | Linux: the game does not start or the picture is broken | The game needs a Vulkan 1.3 driver with mesh shaders. Check with `vulkaninfo \| grep mesh`: it should list `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`. Update Mesa or the NVIDIA driver | | Steam Deck: the game freezes and closes in Kokiri Forest or the Great Deku Tree (`gfx_0.0.0 timeout` in `journalctl -k`) | `RX_VK_MESH_NOCULL=2c56dc1006942f74` in `hookshot_env.txt` gets past it with every model drawn (the culling pass that runs for seconds is turned off). `RX_VK_SKIP_CODE=2c56dc1006942f74` also gets past it, but the models those draws make go missing (see the [development guide](docs/development.md#switches-for-testing-and-debugging), [#817](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/817)) | | "Your antivirus removed part of the build tools" | A false alarm on unsigned programs. Restore the files from Windows Security's Protection history, or add `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder` to its exclusions, then press **Repair** | | Stutter the first time you see something | Normal for now: shaders are being prepared. It gets better when you pass through the same place again | | Windows, NVIDIA: stutter every start in places you have seen, after the shaders were prepared | The driver's shader cache is too small to keep them all (the first start builds about 2 GB of pipelines into it). In the NVIDIA Control Panel, Manage 3D settings, set **Shader Cache Size** to **Unlimited** (or 10 GB). On Linux the game raises the driver's limit itself | | The game is in the wrong language | Change the code in `language.txt` in the game folder. The file lists them all | If the problem continues, [report it](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/new/choose) with the version, where you were in the game, your graphics card, `hookshot_log.txt` and a screenshot or video. Never send game files. #### Low FPS or stutter Walk through the same spot twice after shader preparation finishes. Note whether the slowdown clears on the second pass or lasts until you restart the game. For a slowdown after an update, compare the same spot and settings on both versions if you still have the earlier build. Turn off **Frame generation** for both runs so the FPS reflects game frames, and keep the resolution, upscaler and frame rate cap the same. Attach the log from the slow run and, if available, the one from the earlier build. Say where the FPS dropped and keep the lines around the drop that show `presents`, `GPU time`, `waits for shaders or pipelines`, `VRAM:` and `memory heaps`. Compare total and per-heap memory use with the driver's allowances. The texture cache has a separate budget on the `VRAM:` line. ## Mods Put mods in a `mods` folder in the game folder, beside `hookshot.exe` (or point `HOS_MODS` at another folder), in the layout emulators use: `mods//romfs/...` holds files that replace or add to the game's own. Deeper layouts such as `mods/contents//<name>/romfs` work too. A folder whose name starts with `-` or `_` is off. When two mods have the same file, the one whose folder name sorts last wins, so name them `01-...`, `02-...` to set the order. Only RomFS mods are loaded. `exefs` patches (`.pchtxt`, `.ips`) are left out: Hookshot compiles the game's code ahead of time, so patching its instructions would need a rebuild. The log (`hookshot_log.txt`) names each mod and the files read from it. A mod file larger than the game's own does not load unless the resource size table allows for it: `System/Resource/ResourceSizeTable.Product.111.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.rsizetable.zs` gives each file the memory the game sets aside for it (by the CRC32 of its path without `.zs`; for a texture, its decompressed size + 280). Past that, the game goes on without the mod's file, or a loading screen waits for good. A mod that makes files bigger (HD textures, longer parameter files) ships the table with its entries grown. Since only one mod's table is used, mods that each grow files need one table with all their entries, in the mod that sorts last. ## Build from source For developers, and for players who prefer the command line. Without it the game uses the `image.bin`, `romfs` and `user` in its folder | | `--romfs <folder>` | The extracted RomFS folder | | `--user <folder>` | Where the game keeps per-user data: saves, caches and temp files (and `mouse_sens.txt` when `HOS_MOUSE_SENS` is set; the menu keeps the sensitivity otherwise). Default: `user` in the game folder on Windows, `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux; with an explicit image path, `user` in the current folder | | `--trace` | Log every Horizon OS call (the same as `HOS_TRACE=1`) | | `--prepare-shaders` | Prepare the shaders as the first start does, then exit without starting the game (no build step runs it) | For example, keep saves somewhere else: ```powershell cd "C:\Games\Hookshot" .\bin\hookshot.exe --user "D:\Hookshot data" ``` ```sh cd ~/Games/Hookshot ./bin/hookshot --user "$HOME/hookshot-data" ``` `hookshot_env.txt` and the other test switches are documented below. <details> <summary>AMD FSR 3.1 (every build)</summary> **AMD FSR 3.1** in the Graphics tab's **Upscaler** row (`dlss=3` in `hookshot_options.ini`; `RX_VK_FSR=1` for one run, `RX_VK_FSR=0` never) upscales in place of the game's own network, and with **Frame generation** at 2x its frame interpolation can make the frame in between with `RX_VK_FSR_FG=1` (opt-in: the game draws its HUD into the same picture and FSR 3.1 has no HUD-less colour to keep it still, so the HUD smears; by default the renderer's own makes it). Both are AMD's FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 shaders (`third_party/fidelityfx-sdk`, MIT), compiled into the renderer: no AMD runtime or DLL is needed, and the row offers FSR 3.1 on any Vulkan 1.3 GPU with push descriptors, extended storage image formats and storage writes without a format (`vk: fsr3: ... can run on this GPU` in the log). Its inputs are the scene's colour, its depth, motion from the camera, and the same camera jitter DLSS uses (`RX_VK_FSR_JITTER=0` turns it off); things that move by themselves can trail for now. </details> <details> <summary>NVIDIA DLSS (optional, NVIDIA's SDK under NVIDIA's license)</summary> A game built with NVIDIA's DLSS SDK offers **NVIDIA DLSS** and **NVIDIA DLAA** in the Graphics tab's **Upscaler** row on NVIDIA RTX cards (`dlss=` in `hookshot_options.ini`, `RX_VK_DLSS=0/1/2` for one run): DLSS Super Resolution in place of the game's own upscaler, with camera jitter (**NVIDIA Reflex** needs no SDK and is in every build). NVIDIA's files are NVIDIA's, under its own license, the [NVIDIA RTX SDKs license](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/9981c6350dc58c0ce21f024fd65e31e851c31689/LICENSE.txt). Hookshot never includes or redistributes them: each build downloads them for itself, and only after you accept that license. Never share a game folder built with them, and do not post builds made with them. - **Windows, the Hookshot Builder:** tick **NVIDIA DLSS (downloads NVIDIA's SDK under NVIDIA's license)** before you build. It is off by default and shows NVIDIA's license when you tick it. The build downloads the SDK into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder\ngx-sdk` and puts DLSS's runtime, `nvngx_dlss.dll`, in the game folder's `ngx` folder. - **Windows, the command line:** `python -I scripts/ngx_sdk.py --platform windows <sdk folder>` asks you to accept NVIDIA's license (or pass `--accept-nvidia-license`) and fetches the headers, `nvsdk_ngx_s.lib` and `nvngx_dlss.dll`, each checked against its SHA-256. Then build with `HOOKSHOT_NGX_SDK=<sdk folder>`: `make_game.py` copies `nvngx_dlss.dll` into `<game folder>\ngx`. NGX is also pointed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Hookshot\ngx`, and at `RX_VK_DLSS_DIR` when it is set, and uses the newest `nvngx_dlss.dll` it finds across them (to try a given one, make sure no other folder has a newer one). Never copy NGX's core, `_nvngx.dll`, beside the game: it comes with NVIDIA's driver. - **Linux, the Hookshot Builder (the AppImage):** the same tick as on Windows, and nothing else to do: no variable is passed to the AppImage and no file is copied by hand. The build downloads the SDK into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hookshot/builder/ngx-sdk` (`~/.local/share/hookshot/builder/ngx-sdk`), builds the game with it and puts DLSS's runtime, `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.<version>`, in the game folder's `ngx` folder. - **Linux, a build from source:** `scripts/linux/ngx-sdk.sh <sdk folder>` (it runs `scripts/ngx_sdk.py --platform linux`) asks you to accept NVIDIA's license and fetches `libnvsdk_ngx.a` for the build and `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.<version>`, DLSS's runtime. Then run the build with `HOOKSHOT_NGX_SDK=<sdk folder>` set: `make_game.py` puts the runtime in the game folder's `ngx` folder. NGX's core comes with NVIDIA's Linux driver. - **Linux, a game folder with other than plain English letters in its path:** NVIDIA's NGX on Linux loads DLSS's runtime only from a folder whose whole path is ASCII. A game in `~/Games/Zelda` needs nothing more. A game in a folder such as `~/Games/Zelda-Café` (the `é` is not ASCII) cannot use the runtime in its own `ngx` folder, and the log and the Insert menu say so: copy `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.*` from there into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hookshot/ngx` (`~/.local/share/hookshot/ngx`), which the game also looks in, or into any other folder with an ASCII path and name that folder in `RX_VK_DLSS_DIR`. The **DLSS model** row chooses DLSS's network, by NVIDIA's preset letter, for every mode: **Transformer (K)**, the transformer model and the one tested most here (the default); **Transformer 2 (M)**, NVIDIA's second-generation transformer as it picks it for Performance; **Transformer 2 (L)**, the same generation as tuned for Ultra Performance; **NVIDIA default**, which lets DLSS's runtime pick for each mode, so it can change with a runtime update. The runtime the SDK comes with (310.9.16) has all of them. A change applies at once, without a restart (`dlss_model=` in `hookshot_options.ini`, 0 to 3 in that order). `RX_VK_DLSS_PRESET=<letter>` (or `0` for NVIDIA's default) chooses the preset for one run and wins over the row; the log's `vk: NVIDIA DLSS: ... preset <letter>` line says which one was asked for, and with `RX_VK_DLSS_LOG=1` NGX's own `Using App hint Preset <letter>` lines say which it took. **8 GB cards:** DLAA draws the 3D at full size, and DLSS and DLAA add images of their own beside the game's. In busy areas that can pass what the driver allows the game, and the game then stutters: Quality or Balanced is safer there. The log's `vk: status:` line every 600 frames shows the video memory in use of the allowance, with DLSS's details (its images' size, the jitter and the actor motion) appended while it draws, and a `vk: over the driver's video-memory allowance` line says when the game passed it. The game's log says whether DLSS started, and why not when it did not (`vk: NVIDIA DLSS:` lines in `hookshot_log.txt`). NGX starts on demand: when the Insert menu first opens (to know whether the Upscaler can offer DLSS) or at the first gameplay upscale with DLSS chosen, so on the title screen the log has no NGX lines yet. With `RX_VK_DLSS_LOG=1` NGX's own lines go there too (`ngx:`). Some of them look like errors but are not: `failed to load NGXCore: 126` (twice) is NVIDIA's library looking for `_nvngx.dll` and `nvngx.dll` beside the game, which are not there on purpose, before it loads the driver's; `Feature ... failed to load from cache` is NGX finding no model of its own downloads (`C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA\NGX\models`) before it uses the game folder's `nvngx_dlss.dll`. </details> <details> <summary>AMD FSR 4 (optional, AMD's DLLs not included)</summary> A game built with FSR 4 offers **AMD FSR 4** and **AMD FSR 4 Native AA** in the Graphics tab's **Upscaler** row: AMD's machine-learned temporal upscaler in place of the game's own, on the same inputs as DLSS (the scene's colour and depth, the camera's and the characters' motion, and the camera jitter). Native AA draws the 3D at full size and smooths its edges. Unlike FSR 3.1 (above), it runs AMD's own DLLs, so it needs them beside the game. Choose it in the menu (`dlss=4` or `5` in `hookshot_options.ini`, `RX_VK_FSR4=1` or `2` for one run, `RX_VK_FSR4=0` to leave it out). - **Windows, the Hookshot Builder:** tick **AMD FSR 4** before you build. It shows AMD's license first and stays ticked only if you accept; the build then fetches AMD's DLLs for you (below), into the builder's `ffx-sdk` folder and the game folder. - **The command line:** `make_game.py --fsr` (or `HOOKSHOT_FSR=1` for `nx2/build.py`). Rebuilding a folder built with it (`--update`) keeps it; `--no-fsr` takes it out. - **AMD's files:** Hookshot includes only AMD's MIT-licensed API headers (`third_party/fidelityfx`). Put `amd_fidelityfx_loader_vk.dll` and `amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_vk.dll` from the [FidelityFX SDK](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK) 2.4 release (`Kits/FidelityFX/signedbin`) beside the game's exe (`bin\hookshot.exe`) or in the game folder. (`RX_VK_FSR_DIR` names another folder, for testing: set it in the environment or a `HOS_ENV_FILE` file; `hookshot_env.txt` takes no paths.) Without them the Upscaler row says so and offers the rest. On Linux, a Vulkan FSR 4 library (`amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_vk.so`, such as fsr4-vk's) takes their place. - **Or fetched for you (Windows):** `make_game.py --fsr --fetch-fsr-runtime --accept-amd-license` downloads those two DLLs and AMD's license from AMD's FidelityFX SDK repository at the v2.4.0 tag, checks each against its SHA-256, and puts them in the game folder (`HOOKSHOT_FFX_SDK=<folder>` keeps them between builds, default `work fx-sdk`). `python -I scripts/ffx_sdk.py --accept-amd-license --game <game folder>` does the same for a game built already. Without `--accept-amd-license` nothing is downloaded (the script asks when run by hand), as with NVIDIA's license for DLSS. AMD DLLs already in the game folder that are not v2.4.0's (a newer SDK put there by hand) are left alone, and the build says so. They are AMD's, under [AMD's FSR SDK license](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/blob/7539ae8b6568ad29ed78a753404351daf3b5cca7/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/license.md) (`LICENSE-AMD-FSR-SDK.md` beside them). On Linux the flag does nothing but say so. The log's `vk: AMD FSR 4:` lines say which of AMD's upscalers it found for the card and which it uses (the newest FSR 4; never an older FSR in its place), and why not when it did not start. Tested on an RX 6700 XT (RDNA 2). </details> <details> <summary>Switches for testing (hookshot_env.txt)</summary> Switches to test (`RX_VK_NOOPT=1` and the others) go in `hookshot_env.txt` in the game folder, one `NAME=VALUE` a line, on Windows and Linux. The running game reads it, not the builder. A test run can name another file with `HOS_ENV_FILE=<path>`; the game then reads that one instead and leaves `hookshot_env.txt` alone. `hookshot_env.txt` sets only the game's own switches (names that start with `RX_`, `HOS_`, `HOOKSHOT_`, `EDEN_`, `NVN_`, `TOTK_` or `SDL_`, but not SDL's library names such as `SDL_VULKAN_LIBRARY`), and no value that is a path except `RX_VK_DLSS_DIR`'s (a folder on this PC, not a network share), and no value at all for the switches that name a file or folder (`HOS_AUDIO_DUMP`, `RX_VK_SHOTS` and the like) or press buttons on a timer (`HOS_INPUT_SCRIPT`, `RX_VK_MENU_SCRIPT`); other lines are left out, and the log says so. Switches that need a path, or other variables, go in a file named by `HOS_ENV_FILE`. To enable the debug tools, turn **Debug tools** on in the menu's Debug tab (or add `HOS_OOT_CHEATS=1` to `hookshot_env.txt` in the game folder). The tools then show below it on the same tab. The tab's Developer section, always shown, has the Descriptor reuse and Sampler cache rows. `RX_VK_UI_GAME_FONT=0` draws the menu with the included font (Libertinus) even when the game's files have the game's own menu font. `RX_VK_UI_PROMPTS=pad` (or `keys`) shows the controller's (or the keyboard's) prompts whatever was used last, for screenshots. For a first run on a 4 GB card such as a GTX 1650, `RX_VK_LOW_SPEC=1` starts with the Minimum (4GB) preset, with frame generation and upscaling off. It applies only when there is no `hookshot_options.ini` yet; after that, change the settings in the in-game menu. `RX_VK_MOVIE_UPSCALE=linear` replaces the movies' neural upscale with the plain linear one. The default, `auto`, keeps the networks and falls back only when a movie frame takes the GPU more than 40 ms. That is on NVIDIA cards: on other cards, or where the GPU cannot multiply the networks' matrices itself, the movies always get the linear upscale. It does not change the gameplay upscaler, and movies can look softer. `RX_VK_NETWORK_KEEP=all` takes precedence and keeps the movie networks. `RX_VK_SKIP_CODE=<prefix,...>` leaves out the draws of every program with a stage whose native code key starts with one of the prefixes (the keys the log prints after "its code:"). On a Steam Deck, `RX_VK_SKIP_CODE=2c56dc1006942f74` avoids a GPU hang in Kokiri Forest and the Great Deku Tree: the GPU runs for seconds in the programs that share that task shader (a culling pass) until the kernel resets it ([#817](https://github.com/NotRexed/Hookshot/issues/817)). It is a workaround, not a fix: those are task + mesh programs, so the geometry they draw goes with them, and key models are missing while it is set. Off unless set. The switches for scripted test runs, screenshots, frame dumps and profiles are in the [development guide](docs/development.md#switches-for-testing-and-debugging). `RX_VK_WB_MAX_KB=<KB>` stops the write-back of written GPU bindings larger than that. OoT writes tens of MB of culling lists and per-frame buffers through the GPU that the CPU never reads, and copying them back sat on every submit's memory sync: in Hyrule Field on a 10 GB RTX 3080, about 66 MB and 4.4 ms a submit, holding the scene at 45-48 fps. `RX_VK_WB_MAX_KB=1024` still copies the small results the CPU does read (the exposure meter and the like) and took the same scene to 59-60 fps. `0` or unset copies every written binding, as before. </details> ## How it works 1. `nx2/lift.py` translates the game's ARM64 code to C. 2. `nx2/build.py` compiles that C together with `host/`, which plays the part of the console's system. 3. `host/nvn_native.c` records the game's NVN2 graphics calls, and `gpu/vk/` replays them on Vulkan. 4. Switch 2 Ampere shaders are lowered to Maxwell (`lower_to_maxwell.h`) and translated to SPIR-V by Eden's shader recompiler. More detail is in the [development guide](docs/development.md) and the [design notes](docs/design.md). ## Want to help? Testing on other graphics cards and reporting the result already helps a lot, and so does playing further into the game than anyone has yet. Bigger ways to help: - **Linux testing.** The Linux build (`host/posix`)

title: Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
author: Jakeschincariol
body:
# The Replica skill

Eleven Claude skills that clone any app. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key,
nothing to connect.

One reverse-engineers the app you want to clone. One rebuilds it. One tests it
for bugs. And one is the Entrepreneur: it reads what the app's users hate and
fixes it in yours, so you have an app you can sell.

In between, the others plan the stack and the database, rebuild the design
system, wire up auth and payments, score your clone against the original, give
it a name and a brand of its own, write the landing page and the store
listing, and put it live on your domain.

**It rebuilds what an app does, never what it owns.** Features and flows,
clean-room style. Not its code, its logo, its copy or its content. The
fine print is at the bottom, and the skills enforce it.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
/plugin install replica-skill@replica-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/replica-skill:replica-recon` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/replica-recon`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.git
cp -r replica-skill/replica-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the
method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/replica-recon` | Reverse-engineers any app: screens, flows, components, data model. From public pages, screenshots, store listings and your own account. |
| `/replica-architect` | Plans the stack, database schema and API for your clone. |
| `/replica-design` | Rebuilds the design system: colours, type, spacing, components. As tokens, with your own assets. |
| `/replica-build` | Rebuilds the app screen by screen from the recon map. |
| `/replica-backend` | Auth, database, payments and integrations. |
| `/replica-test` | Clicks through every flow and tests it for bugs. |
| `/replica-diff` | Compares your clone against the original. A parity score and what is missing. |
| `/replica-entrepreneur` | Reads what the app's users hate in real reviews and turns it into fixes and a positioning angle. |
| `/replica-brand` | Names and rebrands your version so it is yours. |
| `/replica-launch` | Landing page, pricing and App Store listing. |
| `/replica-deploy` | Ships it live on your own domain. |

## How to use it

Run them in order. Each one reads what the last one wrote, in a `replica/`
folder in your project.

```
recon -> architect -> design -> build -> backend -> test -> diff -> entrepreneur -> brand -> launch -> deploy
```

An example: cloning a scheduling app, the kind where you share a link and
people book a time with you.

1. **`/replica-recon`** with the app's URL. It reads the help center, the
   pricing page, the store listing and public walkthroughs, and you click
   through your own account with it. Out comes `replica/recon.md`: 18
   screens, 7 flows (guest books a meeting, host sets availability, guest
   reschedules...), the components, an inferred data model (users, event
   types, availability, bookings) and `features.csv`. The partner
   marketplace is marked out of scope: that is their network, not a feature.
2. **`/replica-architect`** picks Next.js, Postgres, Stripe and Resend, writes
   the schema (with a constraint so two guests can never book the same slot)
   and orders the build: the booking flow end to end first.
3. **`/replica-design`** measures the screenshots into tokens: colour roles,
   type scale, 8px spacing, the date picker and slot button specs. Open
   icons, an open font, your own words.
4. **`/replica-build`** builds the shell, then the booking flow, then every
   screen with all its states, ticking off `features.csv` as it goes.
5. **`/replica-backend`** adds sign up, Google Calendar through Google's own
   API with your keys, Stripe for paid bookings, reminder emails.
6. **`/replica-test`** writes a test plan from the 7 flows, Playwright specs
   for the happy paths and edge cases (time zones, a slot taken mid-booking,
   double submit), and logs bugs by severity until no S1 or S2 is open.
7. **`/replica-diff`** scores it. Features 86, all must-haves done, booking
   page layout 91. Missing: round-robin for teams, the website embed.
8. **`/replica-entrepreneur`** reads 140 real reviews across the App Store,
   G2, Capterra and Reddit. Top complaints: per-seat price jumps, no text
   reminders, guests confused by time zones. Each with counts and linked
   quotes. Fix plan: flat pricing, SMS reminders, a time zone confirm step.
   Angle: booking links for small teams that hate per-seat pricing.
9. **`/replica-brand`** names it (with the trademark and domain checks to
   run), gives it a new palette, a logo brief and a voice, then sweeps the
   codebase until nothing of the original is left.
10. **`/replica-launch`** writes the landing page around the angle, sets
    pricing against the original's public page, and lints the store listing.
11. **`/replica-deploy`** runs the preflight (tests, parity, sweep, listing),
    sets up production, gives you the DNS records for your domain, and ships
    it when you say go.

You can also run any one on its own. `/replica-entrepreneur` on an app you
are only thinking about cloning is a good way to find out if you should.

## The tools

Six of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.

```bash
python3 replica-diff/imgdiff.py original.png clone.png --out diff.png   # layout diff, ignores colour
python3 replica-diff/parity.py replica/features.csv                     # parity score + missing list
python3 replica-entrepreneur/reviews.py replica/reviews.csv             # what users hate, ranked, linked
python3 replica-design/contrast.py replica/design/tokens.json           # WCAG contrast on your tokens
python3 replica-brand/sweep.py . --avoid "Original App"                 # anything of the original left?
python3 replica-launch/listing.py replica/launch/listing.json           # store limits + copycat checks
```

**`imgdiff.py`** reads PNGs with no libraries, turns both screenshots into
edge maps and compares where things are, so your new colours do not count
against you. It tells you which regions differ, in the original's pixels.

**`parity.py`** weights must, should and could, counts partial as half, and
never scores what you left out on purpose or what you added. Missing
must-haves means not shippable, and it says so.

**`reviews.py`** drops every review without a link. Every quote it prints is
copied from a row you gave it, with that row's URL. Themes with under three
reviews or one source are marked thin.

**`sweep.py`** finds the original's name, domain and colours anywhere in your
code, including inside identifiers like `OriginalAppEmbed`, and blocks the
deploy until it is clean.

**`listing.py`** checks App Store and Google Play limits, ranking claims in
the title, wasted keyword characters, and the original's name anywhere in
your listing.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Fine print

**It rebuilds functionality and UX patterns, clean-room style.** It studies
what the app does and how people move through it, then writes everything
fresh. It never copies the target's source code, proprietary assets, logos,
trademarks, copy or private APIs.

**It only reads what you are allowed to read.** Public pages and your own
account. It never scrapes behind a login or against a site's terms, never
logs into anyone else's account, and never gets past a paywall. If your
account's terms forbid using it to build a competitor, it says so and sticks
to public sources.

**It always rebrands before launch.** New name, new palette, new logo, new
words. `/replica-deploy` will not ship until the sweep is clean.

**"Clone any app" means the features and the flow.** Not the content, the
network or the licences an app owns. You can rebuild a music app's player,
playlists and sharing. You cannot clone its catalogue.

**No guarantee of a "perfect" clone.** Results depend on how complex the app
is. A booking tool is weeks. A spreadsheet engine is not. `/replica-recon`
sizes it honestly before you start, and `/replica-diff` gives you a real
number, not a vibe.

**The Entrepreneur never makes things up.** No invented reviews, quotes or
numbers. Every claim has a link, and the sample size is stated.

**Check before you sell.** Run the trademark checks `/replica-brand` lists,
read the terms of anything you used, and talk to a lawyer before launch if
there is money on the line. This is not legal advice.

## Files

```
replica-recon/         SKILL.md, recon-map.md, features.csv (the matrix template)
replica-architect/     SKILL.md, architecture.md
replica-design/        SKILL.md, tokens.json, contrast.py
replica-build/         SKILL.md
replica-backend/       SKILL.md
replica-test/          SKILL.md, test-plan.md, bug-report.md, e2e.example.spec.ts
replica-diff/          SKILL.md, imgdiff.py, parity.py
replica-entrepreneur/  SKILL.md, reviews.py, themes.json
replica-brand/         SKILL.md, sweep.py
replica-launch/        SKILL.md, listing.py, listing.example.json
replica-deploy/        SKILL.md, preflight.md
tests/                 the tests for every tool
```

Your own files live in `replica/` in your project. The skills read each
other's.

## Credit

Made by Jake Schincariol, [opusjake.ai](https://opusjake.ai). Siblings:
[Arena](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/arena-skill),
[X](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/x-agent-skill),
[LinkedIn](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill),
[Instagram](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill).

## License

MIT. Take it, change it, ship it.
